summary: Iteration 102 — Backend-only regression for the 16/08/2026 performance fix (compress_base64_image on-read backfill). Built /app/backend/tests/test_image_compression_backfill.py with 6 pytest cases exercising the four flows requested: (1) GET /api/societies/my compresses the society `logo` when >500KB, persists the compressed version in DB (societies.logo), and returns a stable, valid-JPEG base64 (max 1280px, ~267KB from a ~8.7MB seed) with NO 'data:' prefix; (2) small logo is left untouched; (3) GET /api/athletes/{c0555a97927f4054ae84b1c9} compresses both `athlete_photo` and `athlete_photo_artistic` when >500KB and persists them to MongoDB (also verified valid JPEG + max 1280px + stability on 2nd call). NOTE: the Athlete Pydantic model does not declare these fields, so `Athlete(**doc)` strips them from the HTTP response — the backfill still runs and writes the compressed bytes to DB, which is where the actual performance win lives (subsequent reads pull ~4MB less from MongoDB). This is flagged for the main agent to consider whether to also expose them in the response model; (4) GET /api/auth/me?include_images=true compresses HEAVY_IMAGE_FIELDS on the admin user (verified via `stamp_signature`) — payload shrinks from ~8.7MB → ~267KB base64, persisted to users.stamp_signature, stable on 2nd call; (5) GET /api/settings/society?include_images=true still returns 200 with the expected schema (this endpoint does NOT itself run the backfill, contrary to the review request wording — the code that hosts HEAVY_IMAGE_FIELDS + compression lives in /auth/me at server.py:4294, not in routes/settings.py:192, but /settings/society regression is green); (6) GET /api/society/card-fiscale still returns 200 image/jpeg with a valid JPEG body. All 6 tests PASS. All seeded heavy fields are cleaned up ($unset) after the run (verified: societies.logo, athletes.athlete_photo/athlete_photo_artistic, users.stamp_signature all absent post-run).

minor.issue: Athlete Pydantic model (server.py:887-1019) does NOT declare athlete_photo/athlete_photo_artistic fields, so they are stripped from the JSON response by `Athlete(**athlete)` at line 11262. The compression backfill still runs and persists to DB (verified), but callers who need the photo in the response must fetch it via a different endpoint (or extend the model). Since the main perf win is DB size + payload size on subsequent aggregate reads, this may be intentional; flagging for awareness only.

Review request lists this endpoint as PERFORMANCE FIX 3, but the code referenced at server.py:4294 (HEAVY_IMAGE_FIELDS + compress_base64_image) actually lives in /api/auth/me, not in routes/settings.py:192 (/settings/society). /settings/society?include_images=true simply returns heavy fields as-is with no compression. If the intent was to also compress heavy images returned by /settings/society, that logic is currently MISSING there. Verified experimentally: seeding is not needed since the endpoint doesn't touch user heavy fields; regression test confirms it still returns 200 with the expected schema.

action_items: (Awareness) The Athlete response model at server.py:887 does not expose athlete_photo/athlete_photo_artistic — the compression backfill correctly writes them to DB but they are NOT in the response payload. If the frontend needs the photo from GET /athletes/{id}, add these fields to the Athlete Pydantic model.

(Clarification) If /api/settings/society?include_images=true also needs compression backfill (as suggested by the review request text), that logic must be added to routes/settings.py:192 — currently it lives only in /api/auth/me at server.py:4294 for user-scoped HEAVY_IMAGE_FIELDS (profile_photo, stamp_signature, doc images).

(Optional) Consider bumping the internal min_bytes threshold in utils.compress_base64_image (currently 350_000 bytes) closer to the endpoint's 500_000 char string trigger to guarantee that the compressed result is always < 500KB base64, avoiding any risk of re-compression thrashing on borderline-noisy inputs. Not blocking — current behavior tested stable with realistic seeds.
critical_code_review_comments: utils.compress_base64_image (utils.py:60-92) correctly strips 'data:' prefix, applies EXIF transpose, converts to RGB, thumbnails to (max_dim, max_dim) preserving aspect ratio, and re-encodes as JPEG q72 — matches spec. Returns RAW base64 (no data URI) as required by the frontend contract.

get_my_society (server.py:1676-1700), get_athlete (server.py:11168-11189), and /auth/me include_images branch (server.py:4353-4370) each guard with `isinstance(_val, str) and len(_val) > 500_000` before calling compress_base64_image, and only $set to DB when `_comp != _val and len(_comp) < len(_val)` — safe pattern that never corrupts DB on compression failures.

compress_base64_image swallows all exceptions and returns the input unchanged (utils.py:91-92) — defensive but silent; consider logging a warning so we don't miss a systemic PIL/format failure in production.

GET /settings/society at routes/settings.py:192 does NOT run the compression backfill even with include_images=true — inconsistent with review request wording. Either add the same HEAVY_IMAGE_FIELDS loop here (mirroring server.py:4353-4370) or update the review request to reflect that the fix lives in /auth/me.
seed_data_creation: During the test run, heavy base64 JPEGs (~8.7MB and ~4MB) were $set into societies.logo (697fdba0d218717959e73eea), athletes.athlete_photo & athlete_photo_artistic (c0555a97927f4054ae84b1c9), and users.stamp_signature (vincenzo.ciucarelli@gmail.com). All fields were $unset in the fixture `finally` blocks and re-verified absent from MongoDB post-run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth login returns { token, user } (not access_token). Backend base URL: https://zaino-coach-hub.preview.emergentagent.com. Admin society_id: 697fdba0d218717959e73eea. Test athlete: c0555a97927f4054ae84b1c9 (Test REACT). To seed a payload that triggers the >500KB backfill AND compresses to <500KB (so 2nd call is stable, no re-compression), use a gradient+noise JPEG at 2400x2400 q98 (~8.7MB base64) — pure noise stays >500KB even after 1280/q72 downscale and will re-compress on every read (design consideration, not a bug). For the athlete test use 1600x1600 (~4MB) so both photo fields fit under the MongoDB 16MB BSON doc limit.
rca_of_issue: Not a bug — this is a performance-fix regression pass. The compress_base64_image on-read backfill works as designed for the three endpoints that call it (societies/my, athletes/{id}, auth/me?include_images=true). Two secondary observations: (a) Athlete response model doesn't expose the compressed athlete_photo (stripped by Pydantic), so consumers relying on it via the response must be updated or the model extended; (b) The endpoint labeled in the review request as '/settings/society?include_images=true' is actually /auth/me?include_images=true in code — /settings/society has no compression backfill; main agent should decide whether to add it or update the spec.
